/-!
# Unfriendly partition conjecture

An *unfriendly partition* (or *majority colouring*) of a graph is a partition of its vertex set
into disjoint subsets such that every vertex has at least as many neighbours in the other subsets
as in its own subset. Every finite graph has an unfriendly partition into two parts (a maximum cut
is one). Shelah and Milner showed that an uncountable graph need not have an unfriendly partition
into two parts, although every graph has one into three parts. The case of countable graphs is
open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Unfriendly partition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/unfriendly_partition)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- R. Aharoni, E. C. Milner, K. Prikry, *Unfriendly partitions of a graph*,
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 50 (1990), 1--10.
- S. Shelah, E. C. Milner, *Graphs with no unfriendly partitions*, in *A tribute to Paul Erdős*,
  Cambridge University Press (1990), 373--384.
-/

blocks.docstring:
**Unfriendly partition conjecture.** Does every countable graph have an unfriendly partition
into two parts?

That is, for every simple graph $G$ on a countable (finite or countably infinite) vertex set, is
there a $2$-colouring `c` of the vertices such that every vertex $v$ has at least as many
neighbours of the other colour as neighbours of its own colour? The two sets of neighbours are
compared as cardinals, so the condition is meaningful for vertices of infinite degree.

claims.decomposer_note: Yes/no question: for every simple graph on a countable (finite or countably infinite) vertex type, there is a 2-colouring in which every vertex has at least as many neighbours of the other colour as of its own colour; infinite degrees must be compared as cardinalities (not Finset cards), and the article's solved special cases and the uncountable/three-part Shelah–Milner results are not posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the mathematically identical proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ for every SimpleGraph on a Countable vertex type there is a 2-colouring c : V → Fin 2 such that at each vertex v, Cardinal.mk {same-colour neighbours} ≤ Cardinal.mk {other-colour neighbours}. This matches the source: `Countable V` covers finite and countably infinite vertex sets; the non-strict cardinal inequality is exactly 'at least as many neighbours in the other part as in its own', valid for infinite degrees (for a countable graph it is equivalent to the 'infinitely many neighbours of the other colour for infinite-degree vertices' formulation); answer(True) is the positive answer and all quantifiers follow answer(). c07's inline form (identical to c02/c08) was chosen because it needs no bespoke definition and so the file contains exactly the slot; I kept its statement verbatim and only expanded the module docstring/references and theorem docstring (drawn from c01/c04/c06). Verified in a scratch file that the inline predicate holds for K₂ with distinct colours, fails for K₂ constant colouring, and fails for an infinite star coloured constantly (ℵ₀ ≤ 0 is false), so the cardinal comparison behaves as intended.

context:
In the mathematics of infinite graphs, an unfriendly partition or majority coloring is a partition of the vertices of the graph into disjoint subsets, so that every vertex has at least as many neighbors in other sets as it has in its own set. It is a generalization of the concept of a maximum cut for finite graphs, which is automatically an unfriendly partition. (If not, a vertex with more neighbors in its own set could be moved to the other set, increasing the number of cut edges.) The unfriendly partition conjecture is an unsolved problem asking whether every countable graph has an unfriendly partition into two subsets.
Robert H. Cowan and William R. Emerson, in unpublished work, conjectured that every infinite graph has an unfriendly partition into two subsets. However, Saharon Shelah and Eric Charles Milner disproved the conjecture, showing that uncountable graphs might not have two-subset unfriendly partitions. Nevertheless, they showed that an unfriendly partition into three subsets always exists.

into two parts, although every graph has one into three parts. The case of countable graphs is

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Unfriendly partition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/unfriendly_partition)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

namespace UnfriendlyPartitionConjecture

/--
**Unfriendly partition conjecture.** Does every countable graph have an unfriendly partition
into two parts?

That is, for every simple graph $G$ on a countable (finite or countably infinite) vertex set, is
there a $2$-colouring `c` of the vertices such that every vertex $v$ has at least as many
neighbours of the other colour as neighbours of its own colour? The two sets of neighbours are
compared as cardinals, so the condition is meaningful for vertices of infinite degree.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem unfriendly_partition_conjecture :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (V : Type*) [Countable V] (G : SimpleGraph V),
      ∃ c : V → Fin 2, ∀ v : V,
        Cardinal.mk {w : V // G.Adj v w ∧ c w = c v} ≤
          Cardinal.mk {w : V // G.Adj v w ∧ c w ≠ c v} := by
  sorry

end UnfriendlyPartitionConjecture

items: Interpreted a countable graph as a Mathlib `SimpleGraph V` with `[Countable V]`, which includes both finite and countably infinite vertex types.
Represented the two partition parts by the fibers of a coloring `V → Fin 2`; the coloring is not required to be surjective, matching the decomposition's 2-colouring formulation.

Expanded the article's definition of an unfriendly partition inline: for every vertex, the cardinality of its same-color neighbor subtype is at most the cardinality of its opposite-color neighbor subtype.
Used `Cardinal.mk` so vertices of infinite degree are compared by cardinality rather than by finite set cardinality.

reviewer_notes: Modelling choices shared by all candidates and adopted: 'graph' = SimpleGraph (standard in the Aharoni–Milner–Prikry / Shelah–Milner literature); 'partition into two parts' = 2-colouring with parts allowed to be empty (requiring both parts nonempty would only change the statement on graphs with ≤ 1 vertex, where it would become trivially false; any graph with an edge forces both colours anyway); vertex type quantified as `Type*` inside the statement (repo idiom, cf. CernyConjecture/SidorenkoConjecture). Candidates c01 and c05 additionally stated the solved special cases (finite graphs, finitely many infinite-degree vertices, all infinite degree, Shelah–Milner 3-part and uncountable counterexample); these are not part of the slot per the decomposition notes and were not shipped. The bespoke-definition candidates (c01, c04, c05, c06) are also faithful; the inline form was preferred so the final file has exactly the one slot. No omission reports were filed by any candidate.
